target.founder: Tim Swift, Mallory Ulaszek, Saul Griffith

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $16M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Roam Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $16.4M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private peers and one public company in the robotics sector, including adjacent-stage players such as Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $16.4M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement, implying a valuation of $33M. Peer-median analysis examined four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with a median valuation of $1.7B (range: $1.1B–$2.0B), reflecting the heterogeneous nature of the peer set across stage and maturity.

The wide spread across methods—from $33M (stage-progression) to $1.7B (peer-median)—reflects fundamental uncertainty in pricing an early-stage frontier-tech company against a peer set spanning from Seed through Series B. The stage-progression method anchors a conservative floor at $28M; the peer-median suggests substantial upside to $1.7B, with a high bound near $2.0B. Key uncertainties include the relevance of Series B comparables to a Series A asset, unit economics validation, and market timing for next-round fundraising. A valuation range of $100M–$600M may better reflect near-term fundraising scenarios, with peer-median serving as a longer-term ceiling subject to execution milestones.
